request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: The best verified estimate we found is a projection, not the realized outcome: CBO and JCT’s February 2011 baseline projected that ACA implementation would reduce federal deficits by $210 billion over FY2012–FY2021 (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). A March 2012 estimate projected $1,083 billion in net insurance-coverage expansion costs over that period, while projected new revenues and direct-spending savings totaled $1,252 billion (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These figures are not an estimate made at the law’s 2010 enactment, and the source is dated 2012; it does not establish actual budget outcomes. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-171441-9f79.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified CRS evidence addresses projected federal deficit, coverage costs, and offsets, but not enacted-time estimates or actual later outcomes. Note the age of source and projections versus outcomes.
